native-jax-import-lm-catalog-disposition.recommendation: Retain the exact-type positive-integer validation and answer the catalog finding with the JSON primitive contract. No corrective source change is warranted.
reasoning: checkpoint_vocab_size is a persisted metadata boundary. It requires a positive built-in int for vocab_size before native_config and the public int return; version and architecture checks nearby deliberately distinguish bool/int/float primitives as well.

A simple isinstance(vocab_size, int) replacement widens acceptance to bool and integer subclasses. JSON true is a bool but isinstance(True,int) is true; treating it as a vocabulary size violates the existing exact-primitive wire validation.

The catalog rationale is type-checker narrowing, but no concrete type-checking failure or unsafe public return is demonstrated here. metadata values are Any at the boundary and runtime exact-type validation establishes the returned int. Existing pyrefly success is parent-reported rather than independently rerun in this disposition review.

Adding a second isinstance check solely to satisfy the lint pattern is redundant; replacing the check with bool exclusion would still widen int-subclass acceptance. A new predicate/helper/framework or guard-mirroring repository test is disproportionate to this finding.
This is inherited source unchanged from public6f9, not an importer-introduced correctness defect. Keeping it preserves the native checkpoint metadata contract.
